# Commit Message Guidelines

## Format Requirements

* Use Conventional Commit Messages
* All changes MUST be in imperative mood

## Types

Types MUST be one of the following:

* `feat` — A new feature
* `fix` — A bug fix
* `refactor` — A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
* `perf` — A code change that improves performance
* `style` — Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code
* `test` — Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
* `docs` — Documentation only changes (excluding: `*.instructions.md`, `*.prompt.md`, `*.agent.md`, as these are prompt artifacts)
* `build` — Changes that affect the build system or external dependencies
* `ops` — Changes to operational components
* `chore` — Other changes that do not modify src or test files

## Scopes

Scopes MUST be one of the following:

mcp, cli, db, core, models, telemetry, config, docs, tests, ci, harness, events, docline, memory, compound, cli-reference

## Description

* Description MUST be short and LESS THAN 100 bytes

## Body (Optional)

For larger or complex changes only:

* Body starts with a blank line
* Contains a summarized bulleted list; complex changes may use a multi-bullet or structured body (grouped bullets or short labeled sections) as long as each bullet stays concise
* Keep every body line short and focused on what changed and why

## Footer

* Footer MUST start with a blank line
* Must include an emoji that represents the change
* Must end with `- Generated by Copilot`

## Example

```text
feat(mcp): add new authentication flow

- implement OAuth2 token exchange
- add refresh token rotation
- update configuration schema

🔒 - Generated by Copilot
```
